title: D.B. Vilensky, Applicant To Purchase Pistol - G. Dicki

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
SECRET
REPORT
Section 2, Special Branch
Date June 4 1934

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE File No. 3-E-REGISTRY. No. D 4827 Date 5/6/34）

Subject (in full) D. B. Vilensky, applicant for purchase of pistol.

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by [签名]

（左侧边注：See also O.C. 25）
（左侧竖排文字：SECRET & C......）

David Borisovitch Vilensky is a Russian of Jewish origin,
born in 1903 at Dvinsk, Latvia (formerly a province of Russia).
He is not registered with the local Finland Consulate which is
in charge of Latvian affairs. Arriving in Shanghai from Harbin
in 1925, Vilensky found employment with the Egg Products Co.,
No. 77 Yangtszepoo Road, as a clerk. From 1928 until 1930 he
was employed with Kelly & Walsh, Ltd., No. 22 Nanking Road.
In December 1929 Vilensky established the Centurion Printing Co.
at No. 126 Nanzing Road in partnership with G. Dicki alias Deeki,
a suspected Soviet agent, who is an engineer by profession and
former employee of the C.E.R. In August 1930 Dicki severed
connections with Vilensky and left for Europe. Towards the
end of 1930 Alexei Ivanovitch Teleshoff (File D.530) joined
the business as a partner. Teleshoff is a suspected Soviet
agent and is reported to be a member of the Russian Communist
Party. He was formerly employed with the C.E.R. in Harbin and
later with the Far Eastern Bank (Dalbank) in Mongolia.
Vilensky is known to be a Soviet sympathiser and is reported
to be an associate of several Soviet employees and suspected
Soviet agents.
In 1928 he was suspected of being a member of the Komsomol -
Union of Communist Youth - and engaged in the service of the
local Soviet Consulate on intelligence work. At this time
Vilensky resided with the late M.I. Stepunin of the Soviet
Textile Syndicate. During 1927-8 Vilensky was on friendly terms
with one Ivan Trofimovitch Zavadsky (Files I.O. 8832 and I.O.8817),
a Soviet agent, who was handed over to Chinese authorities for
failing to register with the Bureau of Foreign Affairs. It is
said that the two men rendered each other mutual assistance in

David Borisovitch Vilensky 系犹太裔俄国人，
1903年生于拉脱维亚德文斯克（前属俄罗斯一省）。
他未在负责拉脱维亚事务的当地芬兰领事馆登记。
Vilensky 于1925年从哈尔滨抵达上海，在杨树浦路77号
蛋品公司（Egg Products Co.）任职员。1928年至1930年间，
他就职于南京路22号凯利与沃尔什有限公司（Kelly & Walsh, Ltd.）。
1929年12月，Vilensky 与 G. Dicki（又名 Deeki）合伙在南京路126号
创办了百夫长印刷公司（Centurion Printing Co.）。Dicki 是一名
疑似苏联特工，职业为工程师，曾任中东铁路（C.E.R.）职员。
1930年8月，Dicki 断绝了与 Vilensky 的关系并前往欧洲。
1930年底，Alexei Ivanovitch Teleshoff（档案号 D.530）作为合伙人
加入该业务。Teleshoff 是疑似苏联特工，据报为俄国共产党党员。
他此前曾在哈尔滨的中东铁路任职，后在蒙古的远东银行（Dalbank）工作。
众所周知，Vilensky 是苏联同情者，据报与数名苏联雇员及疑似苏联特工有往来。
1928年，他被怀疑是共青团（共产主义青年联盟）成员，并为当地苏联领事馆
从事情报工作。当时，Vilensky 与已故的苏联纺织辛迪加成员 M.I. Stepunin 同住。
1927-28年间，Vilensky 与苏联特工 Ivan Trofimovitch Zavadsky
（档案号 I.O. 8832 和 I.O.8817）关系友好，后者因未向外交部登记
而被移交给中国当局。据说这两人在

    Vilensky joined the S.M.P. (Specials) on January 31, 1927,
on the recommendation of H.H. Johnson, Gas Works, and R.P.
Philips, Messrs. Gande Price & Co.    In November 1927 he
obtained a permit (No. 112) to carry a .32 Browning pistol
(No. 162862, S.M.P. No. 1851).    In September, 1928, he made
a present of this pistol to A.A. Saoul, British Jew, manager
of A.A. Saoul & Co., No. 218 Szechuen Road.    Vilensky then
obtained from the S.M.P. (S) a .45 Colt pistol (No.148915, S.M.P.
No. 64) which he returned to S.M.P. (S) on 31.10.31.    On or
about the same date, however, he was issued with a licence to
carry a .25 cal. Colt (No.30325, S.M.P. No. Y.1293) which was
reported to have been presented to him by Mr. Z. Younker Horn
of the Joint Savings Society, 1 Carter Road.    In November, 1932
Vilensky sold this gun to a friend, I.Y. Abramovitch, a suspected
Soviet agent (File D-4827), and a man of doubtful character, who
recently was arrested by the Harbin Police on a charge of
circulating false rumours.    Upon being released he was ordered
to leave Manchukuo and not return.    Abramovitch is at present
residing at 735 Avenue Joffre.
    It is worthy of note that Vilensky after having disposed
of his pistol in November, 1932, continued to operate the
Centurion Printing Co.    This would indicate that the mere
possession of a pistol is not at all necessary to him and
that if he is granted permission to purchase another the
possibilities are that he may sell it to some individual who
is unable to secure one through above board methods.
    It will be recalled that the Centurion Printing Co. were
responsible for the printing of the now defunct "Maskee",

    Vilensky 经煤气厂 H.H. Johnson 和甘代普莱斯公司（Messrs. Gande Price & Co.）
R.P. Philips 推荐，于1927年1月31日加入工部局警务处（特别巡捕）。
1927年11月，他获得携带 .32 口径勃朗宁手枪（编号 162862，警务处编号 1851）
的许可证（第112号）。1928年9月，他将此枪赠予四川路218号 A.A. Saoul & Co.
经理、英籍犹太人 A.A. Saoul。随后，Vilensky 从工部局警务处（特科）获得一支
.45 口径柯尔特手枪（编号 148915，警务处编号 64），并于1931年10月31日归还
给工部局警务处（特科）。然而，大约在同期，他获发携带一支 .25 口径柯尔特手枪
（编号 30325，警务处编号 Y.1293）的执照，据报该枪由卡特路1号联合储蓄会
（Joint Savings Society）的 Z. Younker Horn 先生赠送给他。1932年11月，
Vilensky 将此枪卖给其朋友 I.Y. Abramovitch（档案号 D-4827），此人系疑似
苏联特工，品行可疑，近期因散布虚假谣言被哈尔滨警方逮捕。获释后，他被责令
离开满洲国并不再返回。Abramovitch 目前居住在霞飞路735号。
    值得注意的是，Vilensky 在1932年11月处置掉其手枪后，继续经营百夫长印刷公司。
这表明拥有手枪对他而言并非绝对必要，如果批准他购买另一支手枪，他很可能会将其
转卖给某些无法通过正当途径获取手枪的人。
    需指出的是，百夫长印刷公司曾负责印制现已停刊的《马斯基》（"Maskee"），

Subject (in full) I. Y. Abramovitch, Russian Jew.

Made by D.S. Umemoto. Forwarded by （签名）

The following information has been obtained from the local
Japanese Consular Police concerning I.Y. Abramovitch, Russian
Jew:-
"I. Y. Abramovitch arrived in Harbin from Shanghai on May 27,
1933 with the object of finding employment and resided at No.12,-17
Yamskaya Street, Harbin. He used to call on certain Soviet
agents. He later circulated a rumour that the demonstration
held by White Russians in Harbin to demand a reduction in the
transportation charges of the Chinese Eastern Railway had been
carried out under the instigation of the Japanese Authorities
and for this he was arrested by the Harbin Police. He confessed
that, with a view to securing Soviet citizenship, he visited
Mitrofanoff, Chief of the Harbin Office of the Soviet Volunteer
Fleet, on January 14 and through Mitrofanoff's good offices
he was given an opportunity to see the Soviet Consulate officials.
He claimed that his visits to Soviet agents was unavoidable as
he was anxious to obtain employment. He left Harbin for Shanghai
on February 11, 1934 to live with his wife Ashiya Izraeleuna and
children.

I. Y. Abramovitch was born on March 31, 1892 in the city of
Nikolaeff, South Russia. After graduating from a middle school,
he studied in a medical college in Belgium. In 1914, he was
called up to the Russian Army and in 1917 returned from the World
War with the rank of sergeant-major. Between December, 1919 and
August, 1923, he worked as an assistant in the Medical Section
of the Nikolaeff City Committee. During this period he also
undertook work for the Ukraina Communist Party in the capacity
of a candidate for membership. In August, 1924, he was arrested
by the G.P.U. on a charge of visiting, without permission, the

以下信息系从当地日本领事警察处获得，关于俄籍犹太人 I.Y. Abramovitch：-
“I. Y. Abramovitch 于1933年5月27日从上海抵达哈尔滨，目的是寻找工作，
居住在哈尔滨亚姆斯卡亚街12-17号。他曾拜访某些苏联特工。后来他散布谣言称，
白俄在哈尔滨举行的要求降低中东铁路运费的示威活动是在日本当局的煽动下进行的，
因此被哈尔滨警方逮捕。他供认，为了获得苏联国籍，他于1月14日拜访了苏联志愿舰队
哈尔滨办事处主任 Mitrofanoff，并通过 Mitrofanoff 的斡旋，获得了会见苏联领事馆
官员的机会。他声称，由于急于找工作，拜访苏联特工是不可避免的。他于1934年2月11日
离开哈尔滨前往上海，与妻子 Ashiya Izraeleuna 及子女同住。

I. Y. Abramovitch 于1892年3月31日出生于南俄罗斯尼古拉耶夫市。中学毕业后，
他在比利时的一所医学院学习。1914年，他被征召入伍加入俄军，1917年从第一次世界大战
归来时军衔为准尉。1919年12月至1923年8月期间，他在尼古拉耶夫市委医务处担任助理。
在此期间，他还以预备党员的身份为乌克兰共产党工作。1924年8月，他因未经许可拜访

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / File No. REGISTRY / 4827）
Date May 2 1933.

Subject (in full) Antecedents of I.Y. Abramovitch, member of the Committee
of the Jewish Club in Shanghai.

Made by D.S. Tcheremslansky. Forwarded by DBkm a.

（批：Acc O H 9149）

Further to the reports dated April 26, 1933 and May 1,
1933, respectively on the subject of the Jewish Club in
Shanghai, (File D-4749) the following information has been
received regarding the antecedents of Isaak Yakovlevitch
Abramovitch, a member of the Committee of the above mentioned
club.

He is a Russian Jew, born on March 30, 1892 at
Nikolaev, Herson Province, South Russia and registered with
the Russian Emigrants Committee, No.6-A Hongkong Road.

Following the Bolshevist Revolution in Russia in
1917 he was elected Secretary of the Executive Committee of
the Odessa District Soviet. It is reported that during that
period he was on friendly terms with a famous gangster who
was known under the nickname "Mishka Yaponchik" (Michael the
Japanese) and who played an important role in Odessa in 1918/19,
being the leader of a large gang of criminals in that port.

Another of Abramovitch's associates at that time was a certain
Katovsky, criminal, who following the revolution joined
the communist party and held the post of Commander of a red
cavalry division during the civil war in Russia.

Abramovitch's career in Soviet Russia came to an end
when he was charged with receiving bribes in connection with
the issuing of foreign passports to members of the former
Bourgeoisie who wished to escape abroad with their valuables.

He was convicted and sentenced to death. The sentence, however,
was commuted to 10 years imprisonment which term was subsequently
reduced to 5 years imprisonment. With the assistance of his
friends Abramovitch later succeeded in escaping from prison
and left the U.S.S.R. for China.

制作人 D.S. Tcheremslansky。转呈人 DBkm a.

（批：Acc O H 9149）

继分别于1933年4月26日和1933年5月1日提交的关于上海犹太俱乐部
（档案号 D-4749）的报告之后，收到关于上述俱乐部委员会成员
Isaak Yakovlevitch Abramovitch 背景的以下信息。

他是俄籍犹太人，1892年3月30日出生于南俄罗斯赫尔松省尼古拉耶夫，
并在香港路6-A号的俄国侨民委员会登记。

1917年俄国布尔什维克革命后，他当选为敖德萨地区苏维埃执行委员会秘书。
据报，在那段时期，他与一名绰号为“Mishka Yaponchik”（日本米沙）的著名黑帮分子
关系友好，此人在1918/19年的敖德萨扮演了重要角色，是该港口一个大犯罪团伙的头目。

当时 Abramovitch 的另一名同伙是名为 Katovsky 的罪犯，他在革命后加入共产党，
并在俄国内战期间担任红色骑兵师指挥官。

Abramovitch 在苏维埃俄罗斯的生涯终结于他被指控在向前资产阶级成员发放外国护照
以便他们携带贵重物品逃往国外一事中收受贿赂。

他被定罪并判处死刑。然而，刑期后来被减为10年监禁，随后又减为5年监禁。
在朋友的帮助下，Abramovitch 后来成功越狱，离开苏联前往中国。

He arrived in Shanghai in September 1926 with the assistance
of his wife who is the niece of I. Shainin of I. Shainin & Co.,
a well known local merchant. Abramovitch obtained employment
with this firm and now holds the position of manager of the
"Provision and Wine Department." It is, however, reported
that he received a notice recently to the effect that his service
with the firm would terminate on May 1st, 1933. The reason
of his discharge is believed to be his having incurred a number
of debts.

His wife named A.I. Abramovitch nee Orjikh, is the sister
of Lev Srul Orjikh, Soviet citizen, proprietor of the "Record
Store" Grocery, No.574 Avenue Joffre, who is known as a Soviet
sympathiser and a man of doubtful reputation.

Abramovitch is the holder of S.M.C. licence No.917 for
carrying a pistol (0.25 Colt Automatic pistol), which he purchased
from D.Vilensky, partner of the "Centurion Press", 10 Nanzing Road
a Soviet sympathiser (File D-530). Vilensky is a member of the
S.M.P. (Specials).

Abramovitch is at present residing at No.395 Rue
Cardinal Mercier.

Photograph of I.Y. Abramovitch is attached herewith.

（左侧批注：JB）

他于1926年9月在妻子的帮助下抵达上海，其妻是当地知名商人 I. Shainin & Co.
的 I. Shainin 的侄女。Abramovitch 在该商行获得职位，现任“食品与酒类部”经理。
然而，据报他最近收到通知，其在该商行的服务将于1933年5月1日终止。
据信他被解雇的原因是他背负了多笔债务。

他的妻子名为 A.I. Abramovitch，娘家姓 Orjikh，是 Lev Srul Orjikh 的妹妹。
Lev Srul Orjikh 系苏联公民，霞飞路574号“唱片店”杂货铺店主， known as a Soviet
sympathiser and a man of doubtful reputation（已知为苏联同情者且声誉不佳）。

Abramovitch 持有工部局颁发的第917号持枪许可证（.25 口径柯尔特自动手枪），
该枪购自南京路10号“百夫长印刷所”合伙人 D. Vilensky，后者系苏联同情者
（档案号 D-530）。Vilensky 是工部局警务处（特别巡捕）成员。

Abramovitch 目前居住在梅尔西埃主教路395号。

附 I.Y. Abramovitch 照片一张。

（左侧批注：JB）

Glickeremshansky
D. S.
